Rheithrosciurus.distinguishing_notes: Bornean tufted ground squirrel, the only Sciurini in SE Asia. Unique among all co-occurring genera in its upper incisors with many fine longitudinal grooves (Ellerman 1940; Moore 1959; HMW 2016). Also: very large (HB 335-352; only Ratufa comparable), huge ear tufts (up to 30 mm), pale flank stripe often with dark stripe below, enormous frosted tail, opisthodont incisors, Sciurus-type baculum. vs Rubrisciurus (also large, tufted, Indonesia): flank stripe and grooved opisthodont incisors vs smooth proodont incisors and reddish underparts.

caveats: (1) VERBATIM/OCR: all quotes marked verbatim were machine-checked (whitespace-insensitive) against the retrieved source text, except 18 quotes from OCR-only scans (17 from Heaney 1985, a scanned Univ. Michigan PDF with very poor OCR, and 1 from Moore 1959 where the OCR interleaves the key's right-hand column into the sentence); these were transcribed with OCR errors corrected and fuzzy-matched (similarity 0.73-0.94) to the OCR text. Heaney Tables 2 and 6 were read from rendered page images. Other OCR sources (Ellerman 1940 archive.org djvu text; Thomas 1898; Archbold & Tate 1935; HMW Plazi text) are quoted with their OCR artefacts left in (e.g. "strip3s", "Ground Squirrelis", "79-6" = 79.6, "1s" = is). In Musser et al. 2010 the PDF glyph "5" stands for "=", and "90u" for 90 degrees; in Hayssen 2008 ",100"/".250" are "<100"/">250". (2) SIZE: true adult HB ranges exist only for some species (Hyosciurus, Prosciurillus spp., Rubrisciurus, Glyphotes, Rhinosciurus, Rheithrosciurus, Bornean Exilisciurus, Nannosciurus, and 6 Sundasciurus spp.); elsewhere (most Lariscus, many Sundasciurus, E. concinnus) only means or single types were available, so genus min/max may be too narrow. Rubrisciurus: HMW gives 150-305 but Musser (92 specimens) gives adults 250-305; Musser used. (3) GENUS-LEVEL KEY EVIDENCE: Ellerman (1940) key/group definitions are used as genus-level evidence for patagium absent (all genera), snout not extremely elongated (all but Rhinosciurus/Hyosciurus) and incisors without grooves (Lariscus, Prosciurillus, Rubrisciurus, Sundasciurus). Ellerman predates later splits (e.g. Prosciurillus topapuensis, Sundasciurus robinsoni/natunensis/tahan/altitudinis, transfer of everetti from Dremomys) but his characters are generic. (4) CONFLICTS: Hyosciurus upper premolars - Musser 2010 (primary revision) says P3 present; ADW H. heinrichi gives 1/1 premolars (not followed, flagged). P. rosenbergii mid-dorsal stripe/nape patches - HMW wording vs Musser Table 12 "not present" (Musser followed). P. rosenbergii ear tufts - Ellerman says present, Musser says not present (genus is polymorphic anyway). Lariscus niobe stripes - Thomas 1898 describes three black lines, HMW says stripes not visible; both states recorded. (5) INTERMEDIATE TAXON: Sundasciurus everetti (ex Dremomys) is morphologically intermediate between Sundasciurus and Dremomys (long rostrum, short tail, intermediate bullar lobe; Hawkins 2016); characters given for Sundasciurus may not hold for it. (6) NOT ACCESSED: Thorington et al. 2012 (Squirrels of the World), Payne & Francis 1985, Medway 1969/1977, Corbet & Hill 1992 and Lekagul & McNeely 1977 are restricted (lending-only) and were used only through secondary citations (Musser, Hinckley, Hawkins, ADW, de.wikipedia). A freely downloadable copy of Squirrels of the World on archive.org appeared to be an unauthorised upload and was deliberately not used. (7) UNKNOWNS: cheek_pouches and hairy_soles are unknown for every genus (no source addresses them); tail_distichous, hypsodont_cheek_teeth, dorsal_spots and tail_rings are mostly unknown. Absence of stripes/spots was recorded only where a source says "plain", "patternless", "unicolor", "no ... stripes" etc., not inferred from silence.
